evaluation_cases.query: What was the root cause and resolution of incident INC-NS-0001?
expected_answer_facts: Incident INC-NS-0001 corresponds to event EVT-NS-0001: 'Checkout timeout outage'.
Severity level was CRITICAL.
Root cause was: Connection pool exhaustion in checkout-service caused by misconfigured maximum connections parameter (set to 10 instead of 100) deployed in v2.4.1.
Final resolution was: Connection pool max_connections increased from 10 to 100 and connection timeout reduced to 30s; pool saturation monitoring alert added at 80% threshold.
evaluation_cases.notes: Direct lookup for canonical incident INC-NS-0001.

evaluation_cases.query: What was the root cause and resolution of incident INC-NS-0002?
expected_answer_facts: Incident INC-NS-0002 corresponds to event EVT-NS-0002: 'Authentication degradation'.
Severity level was HIGH.
Root cause was: Feature flag rollout for gradual-login-redesign triggered unexpected Redis cache eviction in authentication token validation path due to shared cache namespace.
Final resolution was: Feature flag reverted; Redis eviction policy changed from allkeys-lru to volatile-lru for auth token namespace; cache namespaces isolated between feature flags and auth.
evaluation_cases.notes: Direct lookup for canonical incident INC-NS-0002.

evaluation_cases.query: What was the root cause and resolution of incident INC-NS-0003?
expected_answer_facts: Incident INC-NS-0003 corresponds to event EVT-NS-0003: 'Payment gateway failure'.
Severity level was CRITICAL.
Root cause was: Payment gateway endpoint URL updated to incorrect staging endpoint in config-service deployment during PCI compliance credential rotation.

Final resolution was: Config-service rolled back to previous version; payment gateway URL validation added to deployment pipeline; configuration change approval workflow implemented for payment-critical settings.
evaluation_cases.notes: Direct lookup for canonical incident INC-NS-0003.

evaluation_cases.query: What was the root cause and resolution of incident INC-NS-0004?
expected_answer_facts: Incident INC-NS-0004 corresponds to event EVT-NS-0004: 'Search latency spike'.
Severity level was MEDIUM.
Root cause was: CDN cache invalidation storm caused by bulk product catalog update triggered massive origin server load; search queries routed through CDN experienced 5-10s response times.
Final resolution was: Implemented staggered cache invalidation with configurable rate limiting; added background cache warming for top-1000 search queries after bulk invalidation events.
evaluation_cases.notes: Direct lookup for canonical incident INC-NS-0004.

evaluation_cases.query: What was the root cause and resolution of incident INC-NS-0005?
expected_answer_facts: Incident INC-NS-0005 corresponds to event EVT-NS-0005: 'Notification delivery failure'.
Severity level was HIGH.
Root cause was: Message queue partition rebalancing during notification-service scaling event caused consumer group desynchronization and message loss across email and push notification channels.

Final resolution was: Notification-service consumer group updated with static partition assignment; dead-letter queue processing implemented for undelivered messages; missed notifications re-sent from dead-letter queue.
evaluation_cases.notes: Direct lookup for canonical incident INC-NS-0005.

evaluation_cases.query: What was the root cause and resolution of incident INC-NS-0006?
expected_answer_facts: Incident INC-NS-0006 corresponds to event EVT-NS-0006: 'Database migration incident'.
Severity level was HIGH.
Root cause was: Schema migration on data-warehouse added NOT NULL column without default value, locking writes to affected tables for 47 minutes during backfill of 12M rows.
Final resolution was: Migration rolled back manually by DBA; subsequent migration redesigned to use ADD COLUMN with default value followed by background backfill; migration runbook updated.
evaluation_cases.notes: Direct lookup for canonical incident INC-NS-0006.

evaluation_cases.query: What was the root cause and resolution of incident INC-NS-0007?
expected_answer_facts: Incident INC-NS-0007 corresponds to event EVT-NS-0007: 'API rate-limit misconfiguration'.
Severity level was MEDIUM.

Root cause was: Rate limiter configuration update incorrectly set per-customer limits to per-global scope, causing legitimate high-volume enterprise API consumers to be throttled at aggregate traffic levels.
Final resolution was: Rate limiter configuration corrected to per-customer scope; integration test added to validate rate limit scope configuration on every deployment.
evaluation_cases.notes: Direct lookup for canonical incident INC-NS-0007.

evaluation_cases.query: What was the root cause and resolution of incident INC-NS-0008?
expected_answer_facts: Incident INC-NS-0008 corresponds to event EVT-NS-0008: 'Customer billing discrepancy'.
Severity level was HIGH.
Root cause was: Analytics pipeline double-counted checkout events due to idempotency key collision in event deduplication logic, inflating billing amounts for affected customers.

Final resolution was: Billing recalculated for all affected customers and credits issued; idempotency key generation updated to include timestamp component; daily reconciliation job added to detect future discrepancies exceeding 0.1%.
evaluation_cases.notes: Direct lookup for canonical incident INC-NS-0008.
